_comment: Hand-labeled sanity-check benchmark for retrieval ranking. Synthetic papers and queries; labels reflect topical relevance judged from title/abstract text, NOT scientific quality. Papers are self-contained (the benchmark does not depend on other fixtures). 'anchor' queries share distinctive tokens with their relevant paper and must rank it first under any token-overlap ranker. 'split' separates development queries (dev) from held-out reporting queries (test).

papers.title: Sparse Attention Mechanisms for Long Documents
papers.abstract: We study sparse attention mechanisms for modeling long scientific documents. Sparse attention improves long-document classification accuracy.

papers.title: Gradient Stabilization in Deep Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We study gradient clipping and normalization for stabilizing deep network training.

papers.title: Benchmarking Retrieval Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: A benchmark comparing dense and sparse retrieval variants for retrieval augmented generation question answering.

papers.title: Retrieval Augmentation Improves Fact Retrieval in Language Models
papers.abstract: Retrieval augmentation improves fact retrieval in closed-book question answering. Retrieved passages reduce hallucination, but the gains depend on corpus quality. Similar distractors can erase the improvement.

papers.title: Dense Retrieval Outperforms BM25 on Domain-Specific Search
papers.abstract: Dense retrieval outperforms sparse baselines on biomedical search benchmarks. The margin shrinks when queries use rare technical terms.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Retrievers
papers.abstract: We study scaling laws for neural retrievers. Performance follows a power law in corpus size and model capacity.

papers.title: Evaluating Retrieval Systems with Judgment Lists
papers.abstract: Human relevance judgments remain the standard for evaluating retrieval systems. Inter-annotator agreement is often low.

papers.title: Answer Normalization Hurts Benchmark Validity in Question Answering
papers.abstract: Answer normalization inflates benchmark scores in question answering. We show that evaluation details can dominate measured progress.

papers.title: Contrastive Training Improves Dense Retrieval Robustness
papers.abstract: Contrastive training with hard negatives improves dense retrieval robustness. Gains hold across distribution shifts.

papers.title: Retrieval Augmentation Fails on Multi-Hop Scientific Questions
papers.abstract: Retrieval augmentation fails on multi-hop scientific questions that require composing evidence across papers.

papers.title: Efficient Index Compression for Billion-Scale Retrieval
papers.abstract: We compress retrieval indexes with product quantization, reducing memory while preserving recall at billion scale.

papers.title: Multilingual Dense Retrieval for Low-Resource Languages
papers.abstract: Multilingual dense retrieval improves cross-lingual search for low-resource languages.

papers.title: Reproducibility Gaps in Information Retrieval Research
papers.abstract: Reproducibility gaps are common in information retrieval research. Seeds, hyperparameters, and evaluation protocols are often underreported.
